# Prefix Sum — Subtract Off the Unwanted Beginning

## The identity to remember

$$
\sum_{i=l}^{r}a_i=P_{r+1}-P_l
$$

**Every symbol explained:** a_i are sequence values; l and r are inclusive zero-based positions; P_j is the sum of a_0 through a_(j−1), with P_0=0.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For a=[2,4,1,5], prefix array P=[0,2,6,7,12]. Sum from l=1 to r=3 is 12−2=10, matching 4+1+5.

## Why it is true

P_(r+1) includes all values up through r. P_l includes exactly those before l. Subtracting cancels the unwanted prefix and leaves the desired contiguous interval.

## When to recognise it

Use in algorithms that repeatedly request interval sums; it reduces each sum query to two lookups once P is constructed.

## Algorithm or number puzzle application

For repeated queries over 10,000 elements, preprocessing takes O(n) and each range sum takes O(1), instead of summing every range separately.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

The index convention matters; P[r]−P[l] means a half-open interval [l,r), not inclusive r.

## Your turn

Given P=[0,3,8,9,15], find sum of positions 1 through 3.

**Memory rule:** Reconstruct the cancellation or counting argument before memorising the formula.
